info.title: Cisco DC Networking App for Splunk

cloud_release.notes:
\- Fixed an issue where duplicate Cisco ACI authentication (\`aaaSessionLR\`) events could be ingested. Session-log collection now de-duplicates objects by their unique id/dn within a collection run and applies a deterministic \`order-by\` query parameter, so records are no longer repeated across paginated APIC responses.

\- Aligned version and packaging metadata across the app.

release.notes:
* Added column sorting throughout product details, related objects, endpoint/path evidence, exact measurements, lifecycle, checkpoint and setup tables, including separate interface Admin and Operational states. Activate a column heading again to reverse direction. Sorting applies to all loaded matching rows before pagination; it does not request extra controller data. Numeric zero remains a value, missing values sort last, and action-only columns remain controls.
* Corrected proxy credential URL encoding across product connections, preserving spaces and special characters in outbound authentication while retaining saved account settings.
* Improved ACI physical-interface status, units and operational-speed presentation, and connected Overview switch details to the existing Inventory investigations without adding controller requests.
* Connected consecutive reported measurements in shared time-series charts regardless of sample spacing. Preserved actual sample markers, series identity, exact values and keyboard selection; missing values are not filled or interpreted as zero.
* ACI health and active-fault reads finish when APIC's validated page total proves completion, avoiding a redundant empty request. Changed child populations restart only the pending parent probe; written-page recovery and controller budgets remain intact.
* Contract consumer/provider relationships correlate on the observed contract parent DN without assuming a reverse-relation name format. Routing views label node/VRF-sharing L3Outs as configuration context rather than implying a unique peer association.
* Endpoint attachment history compares interfaces within each observed node; vPC peer observations are not labelled as endpoint moves. Cross-node migration requires separate source evidence.
* Normally completed, count-verified searches accept Splunk's exact reduced-bucket performance notice. Truncation, unknown warnings and abnormal jobs still fail closed.
* ACI history classes interrupted by a read timeout yield the next branch turn while retaining checkpoints, controller cooldowns and request limits.
* Authentication views exclude collector credential metadata. Learned MAC observations no longer appear as IP addresses through CIM aliases, and zero-result messages apply to both text and field filters.
* Fault Type filters retain APIC’s native type from vendor metadata or original JSON instead of Splunk’s normalized event classification.
* Corrected ACI tenant/EPG counts to use canonical policy identities, reconciled active faults with indexed faultInst evidence, and added native Severity/Domain/Type filters. ACI views use contextual row actions and account labels while preserving controller identifiers.
* Added physical fabricLink topology with observed ports, IP/MAC endpoint search, system-model correlation and per-site firmware distribution. New indexed investigations cover external EPG subnets, contract consumers/providers, node hardware, BGP/OSPF neighbors and PBR/IP SLA evidence. Optional collection stays explicit and missing operational telemetry stays unknown.
* ND partial resource batches now include acknowledged output in cycle event totals while retaining incomplete status and resume checkpoints.
* Connectivity Analysis now distinguishes authentication timeouts, TLS failures, connection failures and rejected logins from fabric API failures, including errors wrapped by the shared ND login client. Diagnostics never expose credentials or controller response bodies.
* Made ND policy retirement reachable from Setup’s disabled-input list and account-deletion guidance. Review reads local retirement evidence without reconnecting every configured controller. Accounts may be removed after a directly created policy’s full retirement proof is verified; disabled safety records and permanent fences remain. Ordinary disabled policies, MDS references and protected migration recovery remain guarded.
* Clarified that ND discovery creates related ACI/Nexus 9000 accounts, lists their identities and explains incomplete discovery sources. Search scope retains explicit monitoring destinations before first events and when indexed-data discovery fails, and includes reduced buckets in index discovery.
* Fixed the narrow Connectivity Analysis wrapper, switched fabric discovery to the documented inventory summary and added safe connection-error categories. ND IP cells link to scoped Endpoint Search; hosted/outbound protocol values display names and numbers. Traffic categories compare the latest service-list collection against the latest ND summary and explain count mismatches without inventing rates or collection-health failures.
* Corrected MDS direct syslog header/timestamp recognition for colon-prefixed messages without a hostname, including optional process text. MDS severity lookups now return one canonical value. Added the SSH/terminal procedure used for a real UDP receiver test, with CFS isolation, verbosity and restoration guidance. New timestamp assignment requires receiver activation; historical event times are unchanged and MDS TLS remains separately unverified.
* Expanded MDS syslog setup with destination-capacity checks, isolated test and restoration steps, receipt-time searches and packet-level troubleshooting. Added Mac/VPN receiver instructions covering address changes, TLS identity and cleanup; live MDS delivery and mutual TLS remain separate qualification checks.
* Protected new ACI events from reserved metadata collisions by preserving device attributes such as index\=1, 2 or 3 under vendor-prefixed names. Historical JSON index attributes remain available as vendor_index. Removed the global calculated index field because it can suppress exact-sourcetype event retrieval even when indexed counts are present. Existing raw data is unchanged; historical records can still expose vendor index values during automatic extraction. Use an explicit, search-local bucket-derived display field when investigating those older records; do not redefine the reserved index field globally.
* Fixed Complete MDS monitoring setup rejecting valid end-port inventories above 1,000 records. The bounded readiness check now allows up to 50,000 records and tests the zones endpoint separately from VSAN inventory. Zoning pagination now follows the configured record limit instead of stopping at 10,000 records, and validates NDFC page-range metadata. Limited coverage is shown before creation; independent zoning feeds continue when another feed fails, with degraded health and the previous complete-success checkpoint preserved.
* Fixed MDS monitoring setup rejecting the supported aggregate-alarm fallback. Readiness now shows all ten datasets and their blocking reasons, distinguishes safety-limit failures from unsupported response formats, and explains how to select a supported subset without weakening collection checks.
* Clarified Nexus Dashboard, including Nexus Dashboard SAN, ACI, Nexus 9000 switch and MDS switch collection paths. Corrected automatic account-discovery guidance, documented blank credentials and retry behavior, and separated account associations from overlapping dataset collection. Direct MDS API collection remains unavailable; existing NDFC SAN collection and independent MDS syslog are unchanged.

Existing ACI and Nexus 9000 section URLs remain compatible; MDS live sender validation remains separate.

Added streamed ACL investigation and expanded Nexus 9000 Syslog & audit with all messages and authentication history. Syslog Coverage avoids unrelated API checks while retaining separate indexed-delivery and receiver evidence. Version 2.0.0 BETA is a major modernization of the combined App and Technical Add-on. It spans the product experience, collection architecture, protected upgrade workflows, search knowledge, data normalization, operational diagnostics, and release engineering.

* Added opt-in local checkpoint resilience across the five collector families. Established scopes can retain progress during KV-only outages and synchronize immutable versions afterward. Initial adoption requires healthy KV Store, one supported Unix owner and updated collector/REST handlers. It ships disabled; installation does not activate it. Local-only and sync-pending cycle evidence does not establish indexing acknowledgement, host failover or production capacity.
* Corrected stale checkpoint backlog warnings on Home and Data Collection Health. Later verified shared-namespace checks now clear older backlog or deferred reports for the same collector, without waiting for each input to finish again. Input collection results and report times remain separate; missing, stale, busy or mismatched checks cannot establish synchronization. Monitoring adds no KV Store requests or checkpoint reads to the dashboard.
* Corrected checkpoint synchronization budgets to charge cumulative KV operation time rather than source collection time. Home and Data Collection Health now distinguish confirmed checkpoint backlog from a deferred shared-lock check, show uninspected counts as Not checked, and retain stale and unverified reports separately. Request timeouts, operation caps and outage backoff remain bounded; synchronization does not prove indexed delivery.
* Added live local checkpoint fallback monitoring to Home and the KV Store & resilience tab in Data Collection Health. Fresh collector diagnostics identify active fallback, pending synchronization and later recovery, with input names, collector hosts, cycle outcomes, reported event counts and log links. Stale or unavailable evidence remains explicit; fallback alone does not guarantee uninterrupted collection or indexed delivery.
* Kept Home and product workspaces accessible during KV Store outages. Setup status now loads in the background with a five-second deadline; failed checks show a warning without claiming healthy service or completed setup. Home reports availability as Unknown when setup data cannot be read, even if Splunk still reports KV Store ready.
* Corrected checkpoint journal coordination for parallel inputs sharing one namespace. Short durable updates serialize safely, while a busy background synchronization pass is deferred instead of stopping collection. Recovery diagnostics report `sync_busy` separately from pending progress.
* Corrected checkpoint reporting across all five collectors using observed KV Store operations. Snapshot-only Nexus 9000 and custom MDS/Hyperfabric collection report `not-applicable`; stateful cycles report `persisted`, `read-only`, `failed`, or `not-attempted`. A failed checkpoint operation makes an otherwise completed cycle degraded. Successful writes are service acknowledgements, not a separate durability audit.
* Added a live KV Store health monitor to Data Collection Health. It checks the dashboard-serving Splunk instance every 60 seconds and on Refresh, reports unavailable evidence separately, and identifies its local scope. Remote collector KV Stores must be checked on those instances.
* Added an immediate Home launch check for the critical KV Store checkpoint dependency. Non-ready or disabled status displays an accessible critical ingestion-risk alarm with Splunk Support guidance; unavailable status displays a verification warning. Data Collection Health includes a reminder to supply customer KV Store recovery procedures, especially for heavy forwarders.
* Collapsed KV Store details by default on Home and Data Collection Health, retaining live status and visible critical alerts. Home and DCH use the same local service check and distinguish recent checkpoint errors from a current service outage. Expanded details show collection registration and configured consumers without reading checkpoint documents. KV Store status appears before tab guidance; simulated alerts have been removed.
* Returned successful input edits across all products, including guided Nexus Dashboard policy updates, to Configured Inputs with confirmation and a highlighted saved input. Retained list search, sorting and recovery visibility in the browser session. Interval fields and recommendations consistently display seconds; failed or partial saves keep the editor open.
* Declared Python 3.9 and 3.13 support in shipped input and REST-handler defaults, retaining the older Splunk python3 fallback.
* Kept ND fabric/switch discovery available when the controller does not advertise interface discovery; reported incomplete interface scope explicitly without advancing its dataset checkpoint.
* Added package source/runtime checks while retaining exclusion of customer local configuration.
* Added a prominent Create monitoring policy action above existing Nexus Dashboard policies. It opens saved-account selection directly without repeating account setup.
* Replaced the managed Hyperfabric sourcetype wildcard with the same expandable selected-dataset source-type list used by other managed products.
* Fixed the product divider grip selector and clipping so the larger centered resize handle appears in the gap between panels.
* Replaced the managed MDS sourcetype display wildcard with explicit dataset output names; configured inputs list the selected dataset sourcetypes.
* Standardized primary actions in green, secondary actions with neutral borders, and destructive actions in red across the app, with shared focus and hover states.
* Matched Home product cards to the Cisco common TA with green Configure Application buttons and compact footer actions.
* Enlarged and centered the product overview resize grip in a bordered handle across all product workspaces.
* Put Data Collection Health tabs first and moved the collector filter before Time range, with scope guidance in a collapsed info box.
* Made the product overview toggle a compact bordered button with a directional chevron and clear Show/Hide product overview labels across all five configuration workspaces.

##### Unified product experience

* Fits all five command centers to the available page width with consistent side gutters. Uses consistent button sizing and spacing for Home actions. Keeps diagnostic version history in a full-width expandable row so long histories do not crowd the modal. Retains the cleaner Home workspace cards and simplifies its introductory actions. Restores the previous styling across all five command centers and Classic Simple XML dashboards while keeping the refreshed Configure, collection health, and other UI surfaces.
* Refined Configured Inputs across all five products with compact rows, consistent typography, smaller group counts, and expandable dataset and source-type details. Search includes the collapsed dataset names, fabric scope, and source types.
* Combined the App and Technical Add-on into one versioned package with one Home page, one navigation model, and one installed version/build identity.
* Added a task-first Home page with upgrade notices, the all-product configured-input inventory, direct collection-health and guidance actions, and five product workspaces.
* Replaced the generic setup experience with product-scoped **Configure Application** workspaces for Nexus Dashboard, ACI, Nexus 9000, Nexus Hyperfabric, and Cisco MDS 9000 and SAN analytics.
* Expanded product details by default in every Configure Application workspace while retaining the **Hide product overview** control for a wider task view.
* Added account-gated task launchers for account administration, recommended monitoring, advanced collection, syslog, migration, recovery, and retirement where each product supports them.
* Added product-scoped configured-input previews and full input management with search, sorting, enable/disable controls, edit actions, guarded deletion, and protected recovery rows.
* Standardized light and dark themes, Cisco product artwork, action hierarchy, responsive layouts, keyboard interaction, and accessible focus behavior across the React experience.
* Replaced command-center side drawers with centered evidence dialogs that size to short result sets and remain height-capped and scrollable for larger evidence sets. Dialogs support sortable and resizable columns, a compact expand-or-restore control beside Close, selectable background dimming, and a persistent **Open in Search** action. Search, product-workflow, and Classic-dashboard drilldowns open in a new tab to preserve the current investigation. Regular dashboard tables retain the full card width independently of dialog table sizing, and shared tables and ranking lists use one full-row investigation pattern instead of repeated action buttons.
* Made Home the primary operational entry point while retaining Application Setup as a dedicated administration surface and preserving established deep links.
* Rebuilt the User Guide from one Markdown source at build time with searchable contents, stable links, paginated and continuous reading, an on-page outline, expandable release history, and PDF output.

##### Product collection and configuration

* Kept already-configured and unsupported Custom API endpoints hidden until their separate filters are enabled, including when no additional endpoints are available. Multiword searches match across names, paths, and categories. MDS Custom API labels describe individual inputs instead of managed policies.
* Validated Nexus Dashboard Custom API access-check samples with the collector's response extractor. Missing record arrays and unsupported record shapes fail the check instead of being reported as reachable; a successful check still does not prove scheduled ingestion.
* Honored controller-declared nullable Nexus Dashboard record lists as successful empty results. Missing fields, malformed records, and contradictory pagination metadata still fail validation. Discovery caches refresh for the updated contract, and access checks identify samples containing zero records without creating synthetic events.
* Corrected the ACI monitoring-area selector's static option source in the legacy UCC Inputs page.
* Added discovery-managed Nexus Dashboard collection. One policy can continuously enroll fabrics, nodes, interfaces, and selected datasets as bounded internal work units instead of creating one Splunk input per resource.
* Expanded Nexus Dashboard coverage for fabrics, switches, assurance, endpoints, protocols, flows, congestion, device security, platform operations, audit, software, reports, and other qualified operational datasets. Optional service failures remain isolated by dataset.
* Updated app-owned React dashboard searches to use fields already extracted from JSON rather than reparsing every event with `spath`.
* Clarified Nexus Dashboard traffic posture when a selected time window contains no flow samples. The metrics now report **No data in range** instead of implying that flow collection is not configured; congestion remains independently reported from its own sourcetype.
* Normalized legacy and current Nexus Dashboard endpoint payload fields before Endpoint concentration aggregation, so bridge domains, endpoint groups, switches, and endpoint identities remain visible across mixed controller data instead of being dropped when legacy grouping fields are absent.
* Selects legacy NIR adapters below Nexus Dashboard 4.2 and unified operation adapters from 4.2 onward. Version discovery prefers the local ND cluster; unknown versions block versioned collection. Public API requests use the connected controller's advertised paths, query requirements, response lists, and page limits. Legacy NIR and internal topology retain explicit adapters. Corrected endpoint inventory routing, Policy CAM grouping, advisory aliases, and capped-page traversal while preserving established sourcetypes and individual anomaly details.
* Validates every ND Custom API mode against controller discovery without a packaged capability fallback. Incompatible saved paths, parameters, or response keys require review; input settings are never automatically rewritten. Authentication host changes require fresh validation, malformed or incomplete pages cannot advance collection progress, and request, permission, and server errors remain visible. Optional resource-specific datasets still require their documented resource identifiers; discovery does not prove access or complete collection.
* Added exact Nexus Dashboard Congestion work units with independent checkpoints, bounded concurrency, interface-level or queue-level measurement, and explicit fixed-scope or current-and-future enrollment.
* Changed the Nexus Dashboard Custom API picker to automatically detect the selected controller version and fetch its OpenAPI definitions. The list shows discovered GET endpoints, collection owners, required parameters, and special-handling guidance, with explicit refresh, cache, incomplete-discovery, and failure states. New selections use the discovered contract for validation, response extraction, and bounded pagination; all saved ND Custom API modes revalidate the connected controller before collection. Supported URL-template selections keep their discovered contract while resource values are entered; unresolved placeholders and missing required query values block saving.
* Fixed controller API discovery when the Help Center browser route returns 404 by reading the authenticated service OpenAPI documents used by the controller's own Swagger UI, including the NDFC schema endpoint.
* Consolidated standard ACI collection into one monitoring plan per APIC account, destination index, and cadence while preserving the established health, statistics, authentication, class, microsegmentation, and FEX collectors.
* Added six guided ACI class-extension areas backed by 47 reviewed non-overlapping APIC classes, account-backed managed-object discovery, exact distinguished-name selection, and an Expert path for uncommon classes.
* Converted newly collected standard ACI API events to compact top-level JSON while preserving existing sourcetypes, APIC field names, and dual-format search-time extraction for retained events.
* Consolidated Nexus 9000 CLI and optional DME coverage into one monitoring plan per account and destination index. The wildcard CLI contract expands to all 10 supported commands with automatic component assignment.
* Added a searchable five-group Nexus 9000 DME catalog covering 46 reviewed classes, explicit exact-object collection, bounded pagination and timeouts, and a separate Custom API path discovered from the switch object model.
* Added Nexus Hyperfabric managed collection with encrypted organization tokens, fixed Cisco API origin enforcement, continuous fabric discovery, inventory, performance counters, audit activity, per-dataset cadence, and optional UUID scope.
* Added Cisco MDS 9000 and SAN analytics managed collection through qualified NDFC 12.4.1 and 12.5.x GET APIs for inventory, alarms, congestion, aggregate performance, and bounded Top-N SCSI and NVMe analytics.

Coverage starts with enabled original inputs. Review policy settings if needed, then choose **Apply upgrade** once. A restore point is saved before disabled staging, existing work finishes before replacement activation, and recovery continues after closing the browser or restarting Splunk. Previous exact-preservation migration receipts remain under **Review previous protected migration**; **Review or repair setup** remains available for protected recovery.
* Keep retained pre-upgrade inputs and the downloaded export through the operational soak and recovery window. Use **Show pre-upgrade and recovery inputs** when exact retained rows must be inspected.
* New Hyperfabric and MDS/SAN collection is not enabled automatically. Create and test the required connection before creating a policy.
* Review field-based searches that parse ACI or Orchestrator `_raw` punctuation. Named-field searches remain compatible across retained and new event formats.
* Review product search-scope macros when data is stored outside the factory index scope. Review data-model acceleration before enabling `summariesonly`.
* Restart during an approved maintenance window before the first Nexus Dashboard automatic handover after installation. The workflow checks that earlier workers have exited before relying on the installed drain guards. Other restart requirements reported by Splunk remain separate.
* Already indexed events are not removed by migration backout, policy retirement, old-input cleanup, or configuration downgrade.

##### Supported boundaries and known limitations

* Automatic handover requires proven app-owned local inputs on a supported standalone or heavy-forwarder collection instance with Unix file locks. Unowned, retained or incompatible collection that could overlap an automatic policy requires account review. Separate accounts, destination indexes and incompatible cadences remain separate. Older exact-preservation migration retains its discovery and contract checks.
* Nexus Dashboard automatic upgrade combines compatible enabled-source datasets into an inventory-enrolling policy and compatible Orchestrator functions into one input. It uses new managed checkpoints; initial lookback can replay data. ACI reuses preserved history identities where supported. Retained originals and checkpoints are not deleted. Restoring previous monitoring can replay data collected since the handover.
* Two fresh collection cycles establish replacement startup. Partial collection errors remain visible as degraded startup and a collection-health follow-up; they are not described as healthy or fully indexed. A failed startup or verification timeout restores original input states. One small INFO cycle audit is emitted even when ordinary diagnostics use an error-only level, without changing that configured level.
* ACI and Nexus 9000 support first-class API collection plus externally delivered syslog. SNMP, gNMI/model-driven telemetry, NetFlow, and APIC WebSocket subscriptions remain optional external integrations.
* MDS and SAN Analytics collection uses qualified NDFC SAN APIs; this release does not add direct standalone MDS switch collection or configure SAN Analytics on NDFC.
* Hyperfabric and MDS managed policies must run on one active collection owner. Local overlap protection does not coordinate independently enabled copies across hosts.
* Custom API discovery shows GET operations or object classes advertised by the selected controller. Hyperfabric uses the current official cloud API publication. Availability depends on permissions, enabled services, and supported response/pagination contracts; missing or incomplete metadata is reported explicitly.
* Generated Dashboard Studio views are retained only as migration references and are not promoted as supported replacements for the established Classic dashboards.

ND IP cells link to scoped Endpoint Search; hosted/outbound protocol values display names and numbers. Added the SSH/terminal procedure used for a real UDP receiver test, with CFS isolation, verbosity and restoration guidance. Added Mac/VPN receiver instructions covering address changes, TLS identity and cleanup; live MDS delivery and mutual TLS remain separate qualification checks.

Version 2.0.0 BETA is a major modernization of the combined App and Technical Add-on. It spans the product experience, collection architecture, protected upgrade workflows, search knowledge, data normalization, operational diagnostics, and release engineering.

* Added opt-in local checkpoint resilience across the five collector families. Established scopes can retain progress during KV-only outages and synchronize immutable versions afterward. Initial adoption requires healthy KV Store, one supported Unix owner and updated collector/REST handlers. It ships disabled; installation does not activate it. Local-only and sync-pending cycle evidence does not establish indexing acknowledgement, host failover or production capacity.
* Corrected stale checkpoint backlog warnings on Home and Data Collection Health. Later verified shared-namespace checks now clear older backlog or deferred reports for the same collector, without waiting for each input to finish again. Input collection results and report times remain separate; missing, stale, busy or mismatched checks cannot establish synchronization. Monitoring adds no KV Store requests or checkpoint reads to the dashboard.
* Corrected checkpoint synchronization budgets to charge cumulative KV operation time rather than source collection time. Home and Data Collection Health now distinguish confirmed checkpoint backlog from a deferred shared-lock check, show uninspected counts as Not checked, and retain stale and unverified reports separately. Request timeouts, operation caps and outage backoff remain bounded; synchronization does not prove indexed delivery.
* Added live local checkpoint fallback monitoring to Home and the KV Store & resilience tab in Data Collection Health. Fresh collector diagnostics identify active fallback, pending synchronization and later recovery, with input names, collector hosts, cycle outcomes, reported event counts and log links. Stale or unavailable evidence remains explicit; fallback alone does not guarantee uninterrupted collection or indexed delivery.
* Kept Home and product workspaces accessible during KV Store outages. Setup status now loads in the background with a five-second deadline; failed checks show a warning without claiming healthy service or completed setup. Home reports availability as Unknown when setup data cannot be read, even if Splunk still reports KV Store ready.
* Corrected checkpoint journal coordination for parallel inputs sharing one namespace. Short durable updates serialize safely, while a busy background synchronization pass is deferred instead of stopping collection. Recovery diagnostics report `sync_busy` separately from pending progress.
* Corrected checkpoint reporting across all five collectors using observed KV Store operations. Snapshot-only Nexus 9000 and custom MDS/Hyperfabric collection report `not-applicable`; stateful cycles report `persisted`, `read-only`, `failed`, or `not-attempted`. A failed checkpoint operation makes an otherwise completed cycle degraded. Successful writes are service acknowledgements, not a separate durability audit.
* Added a live KV Store health monitor to Data Collection Health. It checks the dashboard-serving Splunk instance every 60 seconds and on Refresh, reports unavailable evidence separately, and identifies its local scope. Remote collector KV Stores must be checked on those instances.
* Added an immediate Home launch check for the critical KV Store checkpoint dependency. Non-ready or disabled status displays an accessible critical ingestion-risk alarm with Splunk Support guidance; unavailable status displays a verification warning. Data Collection Health includes a reminder to supply customer KV Store recovery procedures, especially for heavy forwarders.
* Collapsed KV Store details by default on Home and Data Collection Health, retaining live status and visible critical alerts. Home and DCH use the same local service check and distinguish recent checkpoint errors from a current service outage. Expanded details show collection registration and configured consumers without reading checkpoint documents. KV Store status appears before tab guidance; simulated alerts have been removed.
* Returned successful input edits across all products, including guided Nexus Dashboard policy updates, to Configured Inputs with confirmation and a highlighted saved input. Retained list search, sorting and recovery visibility in the browser session. Interval fields and recommendations consistently display seconds; failed or partial saves keep the editor open.
* Declared Python 3.9 and 3.13 support in shipped input and REST-handler defaults, retaining the older Splunk python3 fallback.
* Kept ND fabric/switch discovery available when the controller does not advertise interface discovery; reported incomplete interface scope explicitly without advancing its dataset checkpoint.
* Added package source/runtime checks while retaining exclusion of customer local configuration.
* Added a prominent Create monitoring policy action above existing Nexus Dashboard policies. It opens saved-account selection directly without repeating account setup.
* Replaced the managed Hyperfabric sourcetype wildcard with the same expandable selected-dataset source-type list used by other managed products.
* Fixed the product divider grip selector and clipping so the larger centered resize handle appears in the gap between panels.
* Replaced the managed MDS sourcetype display wildcard with explicit dataset output names; configured inputs list the selected dataset sourcetypes.
* Standardized primary actions in green, secondary actions with neutral borders, and destructive actions in red across the app, with shared focus and hover states.
* Matched Home product cards to the Cisco common TA with green Configure Application buttons and compact footer actions.
* Enlarged and centered the product overview resize grip in a bordered handle across all product workspaces.
* Put Data Collection Health tabs first and moved the collector filter before Time range, with scope guidance in a collapsed info box.
* Made the product overview toggle a compact bordered button with a directional chevron and clear Show/Hide product overview labels across all five configuration workspaces.

##### Unified product experience

* Fits all five command centers to the available page width with consistent side gutters. Uses consistent button sizing and spacing for Home actions. Keeps diagnostic version history in a full-width expandable row so long histories do not crowd the modal. Retains the cleaner Home workspace cards and simplifies its introductory actions. Restores the previous styling across all five command centers and Classic Simple XML dashboards while keeping the refreshed Configure, collection health, and other UI surfaces.
* Refined Configured Inputs across all five products with compact rows, consistent typography, smaller group counts, and expandable dataset and source-type details. Search includes the collapsed dataset names, fabric scope, and source types.
* Combined the App and Technical Add-on into one versioned package with one Home page, one navigation model, and one installed version/build identity.
* Added a task-first Home page with upgrade notices, the all-product configured-input inventory, direct collection-health and guidance actions, and five product workspaces.
* Replaced the generic setup experience with product-scoped **Configure Application** workspaces for Nexus Dashboard, ACI, Nexus 9000, Nexus Hyperfabric, and Cisco MDS 9000 and SAN analytics.
* Expanded product details by default in every Configure Application workspace while retaining the **Hide product overview** control for a wider task view.
* Added account-gated task launchers for account administration, recommended monitoring, advanced collection, syslog, migration, recovery, and retirement where each product supports them.
* Added product-scoped configured-input previews and full input management with search, sorting, enable/disable controls, edit actions, guarded deletion, and protected recovery rows.
* Standardized light and dark themes, Cisco product artwork, action hierarchy, responsive layouts, keyboard interaction, and accessible focus behavior across the React experience.
* Replaced command-center side drawers with centered evidence dialogs that size to short result sets and remain height-capped and scrollable for larger evidence sets. Dialogs support sortable and resizable columns, a compact expand-or-restore control beside Close, selectable background dimming, and a persistent **Open in Search** action. Search, product-workflow, and Classic-dashboard drilldowns open in a new tab to preserve the current investigation. Regular dashboard tables retain the full card width independently of dialog table sizing, and shared tables and ranking lists use one full-row investigation pattern instead of repeated action buttons.
* Made Home the primary operational entry point while retaining Application Setup as a dedicated administration surface and preserving established deep links.
* Rebuilt the User Guide from one Markdown source at build time with searchable contents, stable links, paginated and continuous reading, an on-page outline, expandable release history, and PDF output.

##### Product collection and configuration

* Kept already-configured and unsupported Custom API endpoints hidden until their separate filters are enabled, including when no additional endpoints are available. Multiword searches match across names, paths, and categories. MDS Custom API labels describe individual inputs instead of managed policies.
* Validated Nexus Dashboard Custom API access-check samples with the collector's response extractor. Missing record arrays and unsupported record shapes fail the check instead of being reported as reachable; a successful check still does not prove scheduled ingestion.
* Honored controller-declared nullable Nexus Dashboard record lists as successful empty results. Missing fields, malformed records, and contradictory pagination metadata still fail validation. Discovery caches refresh for the updated contract, and access checks identify samples containing zero records without creating synthetic events.
* Corrected the ACI monitoring-area selector's static option source in the legacy UCC Inputs page.
* Added discovery-managed Nexus Dashboard collection. One policy can continuously enroll fabrics, nodes, interfaces, and selected datasets as bounded internal work units instead of creating one Splunk input per resource.
* Expanded Nexus Dashboard coverage for fabrics, switches, assurance, endpoints, protocols, flows, congestion, device security, platform operations, audit, software, reports, and other qualified operational datasets. Optional service failures remain isolated by dataset.
* Updated app-owned React dashboard searches to use fields already extracted from JSON rather than reparsing every event with `spath`.
* Clarified Nexus Dashboard traffic posture when a selected time window contains no flow samples. The metrics now report **No data in range** instead of implying that flow collection is not configured; congestion remains independently reported from its own sourcetype.
* Normalized legacy and current Nexus Dashboard endpoint payload fields before Endpoint concentration aggregation, so bridge domains, endpoint groups, switches, and endpoint identities remain visible across mixed controller data instead of being dropped when legacy grouping fields are absent.
* Selects legacy NIR adapters below Nexus Dashboard 4.2 and unified operation adapters from 4.2 onward. Version discovery prefers the local ND cluster; unknown versions block versioned collection. Public API requests use the connected controller's advertised paths, query requirements, response lists, and page limits. Legacy NIR and internal topology retain explicit adapters. Corrected endpoint inventory routing, Policy CAM grouping, advisory aliases, and capped-page traversal while preserving established sourcetypes and individual anomaly details.

* Fixed ACI historical collection to resume from successfully written source events, adopt legacy timestamp checkpoints, and retain the checkpoint collection declaration through app deployment. Bounded ordered requests, a five-minute identity overlap, and visible checkpoint failures replace controller-clock progress and silent failures.
* Added observation timestamps and resumable page progress for current ACI health and active faults. Historical records use their original creation time; unchanged health observations remain available on later polls. Interrupted uncommitted pages and the first legacy overlap can still replay records.
* Preserved original historical checkpoint identities during protected ACI plan consolidation and backout. Replacement plans retain the original keys and ownership locks; missing receipts, mapping drift, or pre-existing independent replacement checkpoints require review.
* Fixed Nexus 9000 neighbor topology, multi-command component ownership, DME query validation, and grouped exact-class selection.
* Fixed MDS/NDFC authentication reporting, fabric identity, SAN Analytics fabric recovery, inventory readiness, policy editing, congestion ingestion, and bounded alarm degradation reporting.
* Fixed Nexus Dashboard Orchestrator serialization, software-history event shaping, migration continuity, Congestion review layout, recovery-row visibility, and retirement performance.
* Fixed Nexus Dashboard fabric discovery so events without `fabricName` do not create a selectable **Null** command-center filter.
* Fixed dashboard search macro regressions, ACI `tstats` host filtering, bucketed timecharts, source-type parsing, event-type index scope, saved-search thresholds, and lookup contracts.
* Fixed default-input provisioning, account-dependent form states, proxy toggles, field resets, product icon routing, action alignment, responsive wrapping, and configured-input grouping.

##### Upgrade and compatibility notes

* Back up the current app, local configuration, encrypted credentials, and app-owned KV Store collections before installing 2.0.0. A migration restore point protects one transaction and is not a replacement for that backup.
* Install the App and Technical Add-on as one versioned package. Do not overlay only selected files.
* Existing inputs continue unchanged until an operator explicitly creates, migrates, restores, retires, removes, enables, or disables a configuration.
* Open **Setup & upgrade**, review each detected product, and choose **Review automatic upgrade**. You can also open **Configure Application** from Home and use **Review automatic upgrade** under **Upgrade existing monitoring**, without entering Setup. This entry appears for enabled earlier-release ND, ACI or Nexus 9000 inputs when account and input inventory are available; it invites review and does not establish migration eligibility. Coverage starts with enabled original inputs. Review policy settings if needed, then choose **Apply upgrade** once. A restore point is saved before disabled staging, existing work finishes before replacement activation, and recovery continues after closing the browser or restarting Splunk. Previous exact-preservation migration receipts remain under **Review previous protected migration**; **Review or repair setup** remains available for protected recovery.
* Keep retained pre-upgrade inputs and the downloaded export through the operational soak and recovery window. Use **Show pre-upgrade and recovery inputs** when exact retained rows must be inspected.
* New Hyperfabric and MDS/SAN collection is not enabled automatically. Create and test the required connection before creating a policy.
* Review field-based searches that parse ACI or Orchestrator `_raw` punctuation. Named-field searches remain compatible across retained and new event formats.
* Review product search-scope macros when data is stored outside the factory index scope. Review data-model acceleration before enabling `summariesonly`.
* Restart during an approved maintenance window before the first Nexus Dashboard automatic handover after installation. The workflow checks that earlier workers have exited before relying on the installed drain guards. Other restart requirements reported by Splunk remain separate.
* Already indexed events are not removed by migration backout, policy retirement, old-input cleanup, or configuration downgrade.

##### Supported boundaries and known limitations

* Automatic handover requires proven app-owned local inputs on a supported standalone or heavy-forwarder collection instance with Unix file locks. Unowned, retained or incompatible collection that could overlap an automatic policy requires account review. Separate accounts, destination indexes and incompatible cadences remain separate. Older exact-preservation migration retains its discovery and contract checks.
* Nexus Dashboard automatic upgrade combines compatible enabled-source datasets into an inventory-enrolling policy and compatible Orchestrator functions into one input. It uses new managed checkpoints; initial lookback can replay data. ACI reuses preserved history identities where supported. Retained originals and checkpoints are not deleted. Restoring previous monitoring can replay data collected since the handover.
* Two fresh collection cycles establish replacement startup. Partial collection errors remain visible as degraded startup and a collection-health follow-up; they are not described as healthy or fully indexed. A failed startup or verification timeout restores original input states. One small INFO cycle audit is emitted even when ordinary diagnostics use an error-only level, without changing that configured level.
* ACI and Nexus 9000 support first-class API collection plus externally delivered syslog. SNMP, gNMI/model-driven telemetry, NetFlow, and APIC WebSocket subscriptions remain optional external integrations.
* MDS and SAN Analytics collection uses qualified NDFC SAN APIs; this release does not add direct standalone MDS switch collection or configure SAN Analytics on NDFC.
* Hyperfabric and MDS managed policies must run on one active collection owner. Local overlap protection does not coordinate independently enabled copies across hosts.
* Custom API discovery shows GET operations or object classes advertised by the selected controller. Hyperfabric uses the current official cloud API publication. Availability depends on permissions, enabled services, and supported response/pagination contracts; missing or incomplete metadata is reported explicitly.
* Generated Dashboard Studio views are retained only as migration references and are not promoted as supported replacements for the established Classic dashboards.
